title: Pictorial and Formal Aspects of Shape and Shape Grammars
edition_version: First edition, copyright 1975; Springer lists softcover publication 1976 and electronic publication 2013
relevance: Foundational distinctions among shape specification, pictorial equivalence and subshape; selected early grammar and Turing-simulation passages, with historical restrictions kept explicit.
prerequisites: Undergraduate algebra and linear algebra; additional prerequisites in topic notes

license_redistribution.conditions: No public redistribution permission verified; citation and lawful reading link only.

locators.locator: pp.1–2 and 4–9: introduction and pictorial foundations
pp.117–122: §2.1, formal shapes and rational representation
pp.133–136 and 144–146: §2.3, occurrence, equivalence and subshape
pp.170–177: §§2.5.3–2.6.1, set analogy and early grammar definition
pp.282–288: §2.10, shape grammars and Turing machines

verification.scope: Reviewed 2026-10-20. Read 36 selected printed pages in the publisher book PDF: pp.1–2, 4–9, 117–122, 133–136, 144–146, 170–177 and 282–288, plus contents. Printed page p corresponds to PDF page p+18. Visually checked Fig.2-8 (p.134) and the special matching condition on p.175. This is a reading of selected foundational passages, not the entire 403-page book. The reduction/intersection/difference algorithms, other proofs, painting specifications and Part II aesthetic-system developments were not reviewed in full. The early grammar definition is distinguished from later formulations.
